text: The next hundred billion years. In ninety seconds. Hold on.
A thousand years. The way you talk would sound as ancient as Old English does to us. And the North Star starts drifting off the job.
Ten thousand years, give or take. Vega is the new North Star. Nobody told the old one.

text: A hundred thousand years. Betelgeuse has probably exploded. Orion loses a shoulder.
asr: 100,000 years. Beetlejuice has probably exploded. Orion loses a shoulder.

text: One million years. A passing star barges through the edge of our solar system, and knocks comets loose.
Ten million years. Africa may be splitting in two, with a brand new ocean in the middle.
Thirty million years. Mars tears its moon apart, and finally gets the rings it always wanted.
A hundred million years. Saturn's rings may have rained away. So Mars has rings, and Saturn doesn't.
Two hundred and fifty million years. The continents crash back into one. Pangaea: the sequel.
One billion years. The Sun is brighter, and Earth's oceans start to boil away. The lazy Sun finally got to work.
Five billion years. The Sun swells into a red giant. Andromeda might hit us too. Scientists now call that a coin flip.
Ten billion years. The Sun is a white dwarf: a cooling ember, the size of Earth.
A hundred billion years. Space has stretched so far that every galaxy beyond our neighbourhood has slipped out of view. Anyone left would think their galaxy is the whole universe.
